# Bootc Hypervisor

> Homelab virtualization platform delivered as immutable Fedora bootc images with rootless container workloads and KVM/QEMU VMs.

A complete virtualization and containerization platform built on Fedora bootc (atomic OS updates with rollback). Declarative workload management via TOML configs, GPU passthrough (AMD/NVIDIA), and TPM2-backed secrets. Designed for homelabs, edge deployments, and GPU compute — no cloud dependencies.

## Motivation

Run local services (Pi-hole, VPN proxies, game streaming, AI workloads) on an immutable OS that can't be broken by bad upgrades. Each service runs as a locked-down rootless container under its own system user. The bootc model means the OS is image-based — updates are pulled from a container registry and applied atomically.

## Image Hierarchy

```
fedora-bootc-minimal              Minimal Fedora bootc (kernel, systemd, bootc)
  └── hypervisor-bootc             Full stack: libvirt, QEMU/KVM, Podman 5, workloadctl
      ├── hypervisor-nvidia:rpmfusion   NVIDIA via RPMFusion (akmod-nvidia, CUDA)
      ├── hypervisor-nvidia:negativo17  NVIDIA via negativo17 (nvidia-driver-cuda)
      └── hypervisor-amd                AMD ROCm + Mesa
```

All images published to `ghcr.io/bensmith/` with datetime tags, signed with a cosign **key** (not keyless OIDC) and verified against the tracked `cosign.pub`. GitHub signs with `cosign sign --key`; Forgejo signs at push with `podman push --sign-by-sigstore-private-key`. Both produce the same sigstore attachment — see [docs/ci-image-signing.md](docs/ci-image-signing.md).

Each image carries per-version floating tags using bare Fedora version numbers (e.g. `:43`, `:44`). The `:latest` tag (and `:rpmfusion` / `:negativo17` for nvidia variants) always points at the current stable Fedora version. Supported versions and the current stable are defined in `fedora-versions.yml` at the repo root.

### What's in hypervisor-bootc

The base hypervisor image (`hypervisor.Containerfile`) is headless and includes:

- **Virtualization**: libvirt, QEMU/KVM, virt-install, virtiofsd, edk2-ovmf, libtpms
- **Application containers**: Podman 5, podman-compose, crun, skopeo, distrobox
- **Workload management**: workloadctl (installed from RPM, built in a multi-stage Containerfile)
- **Networking**: firewalld, NetworkManager, bridge-utils, wireguard-tools, dnsmasq
- **Storage**: btrfs-progs, xfsprogs, lvm2, mdadm, cifs-utils, NVMe tools
- **Monitoring**: btop, htop, iotop, sysstat, smartmontools, lm_sensors
- **Security**: fail2ban, SELinux policy, audit, seatd
- **Utilities**: tmux, neovim, just, jq, distrobox, fwupd

Enabled services: avahi-daemon, fail2ban, firewalld, libvirtd, seatd, sshd, tuned — plus the workloadctl exporter timers (RPM preset) and, in the NVIDIA variants, nvidia-persistenced and nvidia-cdi-generator.

### GPU Variants

Each inherits from hypervisor-bootc and adds kernel GPU drivers:

- **hypervisor-nvidia:rpmfusion** — `akmod-nvidia`, CUDA libs, nvidia-container-toolkit, CDI support
- **hypervisor-nvidia:negativo17** — `nvidia-driver-cuda`, more granular packaging
- **hypervisor-amd** — ROCm (HIP, OpenCL, rocm-smi), Mesa, udev rules for `/dev/kfd`

## Workload System (workloadctl)

The `workloadctl/` subdirectory is a standalone tool (RPM-packaged, no bootc dependency) that turns declarative TOML configs into isolated workloads across two substrates: rootless podman containers (the common case) and KVM/QEMU VMs (declared with a `[vm]` section). Each workload gets a dedicated system user, subuid namespace, systemd service, volume management, and optional TPM2-encrypted secrets.

See [workloadctl/llms.txt](workloadctl/llms.txt) for full detail on architecture, CLI commands, and configuration schema.

Quick example:
```bash
sudo workloadctl create webserver \
  --image docker.io/nginxinc/nginx-unprivileged:alpine \
  --ports 8080:8080 --enable
```

## cosy

`bin/cosy` is a separate project (podman wrapper for interactive container sessions). It is synced into this repo via `just sync-cosy` and installed into the bootc image. See the [cosy repository](https://github.com/BenSmith/cosy) for details.

### desktop-containers/ is operator-run by design

The four contexts under `desktop-containers/` (labwc/wayfire × kms/nested) are **build contexts shipped as source, not images this project publishes**. The image `COPY`s the directory to `/usr/share/cosy/desktop-containers/`; an operator builds one on the host with its `build.sh` when they want a desktop, and `cosy` runs it. That is why there is no justfile recipe, no workflow and no test for them: `build-workload-images.yml` and the `.forgejo/scripts/ci-workload-images.py` matrix cover the images that *are* published, and these are deliberately outside it. Building them in CI would produce artifacts nothing consumes — the operator builds locally either way, since a KMS desktop is bound to the machine it runs on.

Two consequences worth knowing. A broken Containerfile here is discovered at the keyboard, not in CI, so treat edits under this directory as untested until someone runs `build.sh`. And the KMS variants need two SELinux booleans turned on first (`seatd_container_connect`, `container_input_devices`) — the image grants no device access host-wide; see each variant's `README.md`.

## Repository Structure

```
hypervisor.Containerfile                  Base hypervisor image (multi-stage: builds workloadctl RPM)
fedora-bootc-minimal.Containerfile        Minimal bootc base (Podman 4 compatible for GitHub CI)
hypervisor-amd.Containerfile              AMD GPU variant
hypervisor-nvidia-rpmfusion.Containerfile NVIDIA RPMFusion variant
hypervisor-nvidia-negativo17.Containerfile NVIDIA negativo17 variant

workloadctl/                              Workload management system (see workloadctl/llms.txt)

bin/cosy                                  Interactive container session wrapper
man/cosy.1                                cosy man page

config.toml                               bootc-image-builder config (VM user setup) — gitignored, generated
                                          by the `_generate-vm-config` justfile recipe from VM_USER/VM_PASSWORD/VM_SSH_KEY
config-iso.toml                           ISO-specific image builder config
policy.json                               Container image signature policy
policy-local.json                         Permissive policy — build-base-local only, never a published image
policy-hypervisor.json.template           Policy template: reject-by-default; sigstoreSigned for ghcr.io/<ns> and
                                          registry.local, allowlisted-unverified for the 6 registries workloads use
policy-minimal.json.template              Same shape, narrower: ghcr.io/<ns> signed; ghcr.io + registry.local open

security/
  seatd_container.cil                     SELinux module (CIL): container_t -> host seatd socket, behind a
                                          seatd_container_connect boolean shipped OFF
  container_input_devices.cil             SELinux module (CIL): container_t -> event_device_t (/dev/input,
                                          /dev/uinput), behind a container_input_devices boolean shipped OFF.
                                          The input half of the KMS desktop pair; both are needed together
  pasta_sandbox.cil                       SELinux module (CIL): pasta_t sandbox-setup perms missing from
                                          container-selinux on F44; remove once fixed upstream
  pwquality-no-dictionary.conf            Disable dictionary check for password quality

systemd/
  emergency-access.conf                   Emergency shell drop-in
  nvidia-cdi-generator.service            NVIDIA CDI device list generator

containers.conf.d/10-pasta-no-splice.conf Disable pasta's loopback splice() fast path (throughput regression)
registries.conf.d/mirrors.conf            Route public-registry pulls through the registry.local pull-through cache.
                                          Installed ONLY when a homelab CA is injected (internal Forgejo builds), never
                                          in the public ghcr image — registry.local is an mDNS name, so TLS against
                                          that CA is what proves the responder is the real cache
registries.d/*.yaml                       use-sigstore-attachments for ghcr.io and registry.local
tmpfiles.d/fail2ban-statedir.conf         Recreate /var/lib/fail2ban at boot (bootc ships /var empty)
ca-trust-inject/                          Empty in git; CI drops the homelab root CA here to bake it into
                                          internal images' trust store (README explains the scheme)
desktop-containers/                       Four cosy build contexts (labwc/wayfire x kms/nested), COPY'd to
                                          /usr/share/cosy/. Operator-run, deliberately not built by CI.
.githooks/pre-push                        Refuse to push `internal` (or anything descending from it) to GitHub

docs/
  emergency-recovery.md                   Boot recovery procedures
  TROUBLESHOOTING.md                      Common issues and fixes
  ci-image-signing.md                     How each forge gets the signing key; the Forgejo sealed-credential scheme
  cosign-local-redirect-loop.md           Why CI signs via containers/image instead of the cosign CLI
  ideas.md                                Scratch list, not a plan of record

.github/workflows/                        build-minimal-bootc.yml (weekly Sat), build-hypervisor.yml (weekly Sun),
                                          workloadctl-test.yml (PR gate), workloadctl-runtime.yml (weekly Mon)
.forgejo/workflows/                       Mirrors of the above (minimal Sun, hypervisor Mon, runtime Tue) plus three
                                          Forgejo-only: seal-signing-key.yml, build-workload-images.yml,
                                          build-hypervisor-f44-quick.yml. No drift check between the forges.
.forgejo/scripts/ci-workload-images.py    Builds workload images from the checked-out tree via workloadctl's own
                                          lib/imagebuild.py; `list` feeds the CI matrix

justfile                                  Build automation (see Build System below)
```

## Build System (justfile)

All builds use [just](https://github.com/casey/just). Key targets:

**Container images:**
- `just build-minimal [version]` — Build fedora-bootc-minimal
- `just build-base` / `just build-base-local` — Base hypervisor
- `just build-nvidia-rpmfusion` / `just build-amd` — GPU variants
- `just build-all` / `just build-all-local` — Everything

**ISO and disk images:**
- `just build-iso-base [rootfs]` — Anaconda installer ISO (rootfs: xfs/btrfs/ext4)
- `just build-qcow2-base-local [rootfs] [size]` — QCOW2 for libvirt VMs
- `just build-all-isos [rootfs]` — All variant ISOs

**Development:**
- `just aio-local` — Build image, create QCOW2, deploy to libvirt VM (all-in-one)
- `just test` / `just test-unit` / `just test-integration` — workloadctl tests (delegate into `workloadctl/`)
- `just test-cli <target>` — workloadctl rung-3 CLI-surface tests
- `just test-all-runtime [target]` / `just test-all-runtime-remote <host>` — the runtime rung, locally or over SSH
- `just push-all` — Tag and push all images to local registry

## Installation

**From existing bootc system:**
```bash
sudo bootc switch ghcr.io/bensmith/hypervisor-bootc:latest
sudo systemctl reboot
```

**From installer ISO:**
```bash
just build-iso-base
sudo dd if=output/bootiso/install.iso of=/dev/sdX bs=4M status=progress
```

**Updates:**
```bash
sudo bootc upgrade    # Atomic update
sudo systemctl reboot
```

**Switching variants:**
```bash
# Switch to latest stable
sudo bootc switch ghcr.io/bensmith/hypervisor-nvidia:negativo17
sudo systemctl reboot

# Pin to a specific Fedora version
sudo bootc switch ghcr.io/bensmith/hypervisor-bootc:44
sudo bootc switch ghcr.io/bensmith/hypervisor-nvidia:rpmfusion-44
sudo bootc switch ghcr.io/bensmith/hypervisor-amd:44
```

## Key Design Decisions

1. **Bootc for immutability** — `/usr` is read-only, `/etc` is mutable config, `/var` is persistent data. Atomic updates with instant rollback.
2. **Rootless containers via dedicated users** — Each workload gets a unique `_wl-{name}` user with its own UID namespace. No privileged containers.
3. **systemd-native** — Generators for boot-time provisioning, credentials for secrets, cgroup v2 for resource limits, journal for logging.
4. **TPM2-backed secrets** — Hardware encryption, machine-specific, safe to commit encrypted blobs to git/images.
5. **Explicit hardware opt-in** — No device access is granted host-wide. Podman must be told to pass a node in (`[devices]` in `workload.toml` → `--device` / a CDI ref), DAC still applies, and SELinux is a third, independent gate that a misplaced `--device` does not open. The base image deliberately does **not** set `container_use_devices`: despite the name it grants read/write/ioctl/map on all ~200 `device_node` types to the `container_domain` attribute, which every udica-derived `wl_<name>.process` type belongs to — the one grant a per-workload `policy.cil` cannot scope down. Nothing needs that breadth. DRI (`dri_device_t`) and ROCm (`hsa_device_t`) work with no boolean at all; NVIDIA nodes (`xserver_misc_device_t` — `/dev/nvidia*`, `nvidiactl`, `nvidia-uvm*`, `nvidia-caps/*`, the complete device surface of the CDI spec) are granted by `container_use_xserver_devices` in the `hypervisor-nvidia-*` variants only, and by name in the `policy.cil` of the three workloads that carry their own type, since that boolean is written against `container_t` rather than `container_domain`. `/dev/input` for KMS desktops is gated behind `container_input_devices`, shipped OFF, the same shape as `seatd_container_connect`. **Existing hosts:** the SELinux policy store lives in `/etc` and `workloadctl enable` rebuilds it (`semodule -i`), so ostree's 3-way merge keeps the host's copy and none of this reaches a deployed machine on `bootc upgrade` — run `sudo setsebool -P container_use_devices off` by hand there. `workloadctl doctor` reports which path a GPU workload is actually using.
6. **fuse-overlayfs hardlink workaround** — Containerfiles break ostree rpmdb hardlinks before `dnf install` to avoid database corruption (see hypervisor.Containerfile).
7. **Image trust is scoped signing over a registry allowlist** — The shipped `policy.json` (from `policy-hypervisor.json.template`) is **reject-by-default, and the default is live**: there is deliberately no `""` scope under the `docker` transport, so a ref on any registry not named in the file is refused before a layer moves. Two tiers sit above that default. *Signature required:* `ghcr.io/__REGISTRY_NAMESPACE__` (the bootc images) and `registry.local` (CI-built workload images) are `sigstoreSigned` with `/etc/pki/containers/cosign.pub`, signatures fetched from the registries themselves (`registries.d/*.yaml` `use-sigstore-attachments`). *Allowlisted but unverified:* `docker.io`, `ghcr.io`, `quay.io`, `codeberg.org`, `mcr.microsoft.com`, `registry.fedoraproject.org` — the registries the shipped workloads and the build recipes actually pull from. Third-party images stay consciously unsigned, because the signature asserts "bytes CI pushed" and never provenance about upstream; what the allowlist adds is that a *typo'd or injected* ref pointing somewhere else fails closed instead of silently resolving. The cost is real and worth knowing: **adopting a workload from a new registry means adding it here**, or the pull fails with "Source image rejected". More-specific scopes win, which is why `ghcr.io/__REGISTRY_NAMESPACE__` stays signature-gated despite `ghcr.io` being open. The root→user local-override transfer (`containers-storage` transport) is policy-exempt by construction. **One thing this policy cannot see is which host actually served the bytes** — it is keyed on the ref the caller wrote. That is why `registries.conf.d/mirrors.conf`, which redirects five of those scopes to `registry.local`, ships only in images carrying the homelab CA and never sets `insecure`: for the allowlisted-unverified scopes, TLS to the mirror is the only remaining check.
